result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A keeps the facts and the suspicion on separate slides and gives the March annual cohort its own slide as evidence that doesn't fit. Its slide titles state each point, and it leaves the test size and timeline as placeholders rather than making up figures. B puts the ask up front and adds useful checks, including the date mismatch. But it spends much of its cohort slide arguing why the result doesn't contradict the hypothesis, adds unsupported details (annual plans 'can't churn month to month', a 10–20% holdback for 2 weeks) and uses generic slide titles. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B presents the March annual cohort openly as evidence that may point to another cause, while A spends most of that slide giving reasons it doesn't contradict the hypothesis before adding a caveat. B's slide titles each state their point, and it adds an opening script and backup slides; A's titles are generic, though A usefully flags that the dates don't add up. Both ask only for a holdback test and stick to the given numbers.
